questions.text: Which payment milestone is source-backed by the 401-402 proforma?

options.text: Payment sufficient to increase total fee payments to eighty-five percent upon completion of Contract Documents services.
A mandatory 100 percent fee before schematic design.
No mobilization payment on signing.
A contractor retention release as the Architect's fee.

questions.rationale: The proforma states an eighty-five-percent payment milestone after Contract Documents services.
questions.explanation: Overspecifies the requirement; specifications typically allow equivalent products unless specific performance requires a particular brand. Attributes budget control to the architect; document detail supports accurate bidding, but does not guarantee bids will fall within budget. Confuses document adequacy with on-site supervision; detailed documents reduce, rather than eliminate, the need for on-site verification. The architect must prepare drawings and specifications that are sufficiently detailed for competitive bidding and construction execution. These documents must comply with all applicable laws, codes, and regulations, allowing contractors to bid accurately without constant clarification. Documents must provide enough detail for accurate bidding and code-compliant execution; excessive brand specification is neither required nor typical practice.

questions.text: What is the safest way to describe UAP Document 301 in relation to the owner-architect agreement?

options.text: It is a construction-contract general-conditions source, not the full owner-architect service agreement.
It replaces all professional service agreements between Owner and Architect.
It is only a CPD registration document.
It proves all design-build work is included in basic services.

questions.rationale: UAP Document 301 defines Owner-Contractor construction contract documents and construction administration rules.

questions.text: What should the Owner do with instructions to Constructors under the checked agreement?

options.text: Issue orders to Constructors only through the Architect.
Issue all orders directly to subcontractors without informing the Architect.
Wait for PRC to approve every site instruction.
Delegate fee computation to the contractor.

questions.rationale: The Owner responsibilities section says the Owner should observe the procedure of issuing orders to Constructors only through the Architect.

questions.text: Which local source is the better owner-architect agreement anchor for this article?

options.text: UAP Document 401-402, because it is the proforma Architect-Owner Agreement covering professional services.
UAP Document 301, because it is the complete owner-architect service agreement.
CIAP Document 102, because it regulates architect registration.
A contractor payment bond form, because it defines the Architect's design fee.

questions.rationale: The batch separates the owner-architect service agreement from construction-contract general conditions.

questions.text: In the 401-402 proforma, what does the Architect prepare during Design Development?

options.text: Plans, elevations, other drawings, and outline specifications to fix and illustrate the project size and character.
The contractor's guarantee bond only.
A PRC oath-taking roster.
A public bidding invitation unrelated to design.

questions.rationale: The checked source describes design development documents with drawings and outline specifications.

questions.text: Which service phase is included in the checked 401-402 basic services list?

options.text: Schematic Design Phase.
Contractor bankruptcy liquidation.
CPD provider accreditation.
Guarantee bond posting by the contractor.

questions.rationale: The agreement lists schematic design as part of the Architect's basic services.

questions.text: Which item is excluded from the checked 401-402 agreement notes?

options.text: Project or Construction Management.
Regular/basic detailed design services.
Schematic design studies.
Contract documents services.

questions.rationale: The agreement notes state that it does not cover project or construction management.

questions.text: Which Owner responsibility is source-backed by 401-402?

options.text: Provide full information as to project requirements.
Guarantee the contractor's workmanship for one year.
Serve as the Architect's PRC supervisor.
Prepare all shop drawings for subcontractors.

questions.rationale: The Owner responsibilities article starts with full information on project requirements.

questions.text: What does the checked agreement say about design-build services?

options.text: The agreement is not for Design-Build Services and the Architect must first secure a contractor license if undertaking that work.
Design-build is automatically included in regular/basic design services.
Design-build is handled only by a payment bond.
Design-build cancels all architect intellectual-property rights.

questions.rationale: The source expressly excludes design-build from this proforma and flags PCAB licensing if the Architect undertakes that work.

questions.text: Which exam move avoids confusing contract sources?

options.text: Use 401-402 for owner-architect service terms and UAP 301 for owner-contractor construction-contract administration.
Use UAP 301 as the sole source for the Architect's professional fee.
Use CIAP 102 to define the Architect's CPD credits.
Use contractor bond rules to decide schematic design deliverables.

questions.rationale: The source-safe answer keeps service agreement and construction-contract documents in separate lanes.
